items.text: Built and maintained an open-source VBA Excel add-in that turns Smartsheet exports into branded customer equipment lists, project schedules, and vendor quote packages, cutting a 4+ hour, several-hundred-click manual build to 4 clicks and about 10 seconds.

Designed eight Excel ribbon tools for equipment lists, schedules, split sheets, and exports, in one-click and custom versions, giving teams a standard build in one click while letting them still tailor the tools to their needs.
Implemented a settings system that saves each user's choices across Excel sessions, letting the one-click tools run from saved defaults with no setup dialog.
Moved the add-in from an unversioned single file to a source-controlled project with a scripted build, making every release repeatable and every change traceable.
Added a GitHub Actions workflow that checks every code change for broken ribbon buttons and missing coding-standard declarations, catching those problems before merge instead of in users' hands.
Created a pre-release check that confirms the source code matches what ships inside the built add-in, so what users install is always what was reviewed.
Split business logic out of Excel-dependent code and added 20+ Rubberduck unit tests, letting automated tests catch regression defects whenever a change breaks working logic.
Delivered 11+ versioned releases, tracking work through 70+ GitHub issues and 98+ pull requests and turning team feedback into steady improvements.
Refactored the codebase in small, reviewable changes, removing duplicated code across five user forms and replacing silent failures with errors users can see and report.

Established the first standardized naming and markup conventions for equipment cut sheets which, together with the custom add-in and documentation, cut the time to prepare equipment lists, customer equipment lists, and RFQs from 10 days to 2.
Wrote the user guide and wiki, plus a developer architecture guide, changelog, and release process, making the add-in ready to hand off and support.

Released the add-in as open source under the MIT License with the client's approval, keeping the company's name, logo, and all customer data out of the public repository while making the tool free for others to use and improve.
Leveraged AI coding agents (Claude Code) to speed up development while keeping ownership of design, review, testing, and releases.
Drafted the add-in's first version with Microsoft Copilot, then moved development to source control and Claude Code, graduating the prototype into hardened, maintainable, and user-friendly releases.
Developed a dual-baseline Smartsheet schedule template through stakeholder interviews, giving project teams a repeatable way to track planned versus actual timelines.
Coordinated cross-functional delivery on capital projects of roughly $1M and 6+ months, involving 5 or more outside companies across vendors, engineering, electrical, sales, and general contracting.
Vetted equipment quotes against the specification, competing bids, and the project schedule, keeping capital purchases accurate, fairly priced, and on time.

Built project schedules with task predecessors and reported schedule changes to clients and contractors, ending constant status requests and freeing the project lead to focus on sales instead of hunting through emails for updates.
Stored user settings in the Windows registry after finding that Excel never saves an add-in on close, so each user's choices now persist between sessions.
Built a Python generator that creates seeded, fully fabricated sample workbooks, letting the public repository be tested end to end without exposing any customer data.

Designed edge-case test data and fixtures around the inputs most likely to break the tools, such as parent/child row groups, wrapped multi-line text, and vendor names that collide as sheet names, exposing failures before users could hit them.
Wrote a manual smoke-test checklist with expected results for every ribbon tool, holding every release to the same check before it shipped.

Defined a repeatable release process, from release pull request through scripted build, drift check, and smoke test to a tagged release, ensuring every version ships with the same checks and updated documentation.

Replaced confidential customer workbooks with synthetic test data that mirrors the structure of real exports, checking the generated files for leaked identifiers, letting the add-in be open-sourced for a client without exposing customer data.
Caught three failing AI-written unit tests by running them, then fixed the test data instead of the correct code, leaving all 20+ tests passing against both real-world and synthetic inputs.

Coached a fellow TPD consultant in adopting Claude Code for engineering work and Claude for client tracking, time reporting, scheduling, and handoff documents and drawings, now part of his daily workflow.
Transformed a TPD client's note-taking from hours of manual work into a Claude workflow that extracts notes from 500+ page PDFs into organized spreadsheets, which they now use on their own.

Designed, built, and shipped an ad-free communication app for Android and the web for a family member temporarily unable to speak, reaching first release in 4 days and v1.0 in 13 days while directing an AI coding agent and owning all architecture and review decisions, giving her a dependable way to communicate throughout her recovery.

Engineered a suite of 458+ tests that runs on the JVM, in headless Chrome, and on an Android emulator, backed by a 90% coverage gate and required checks on every merge, catching regression defects before they could reach a user.

Removed every barrier to adoption for non-technical caregivers: zero-setup preset boards, voice banking with adjustable text-to-speech fallback (voice, speed, pitch), and critical phrases pinned on every screen for one-tap access in emergencies.
Expanded from Android to a progressive web app that installs like an app and works offline, letting caregivers use it on any device.

Improved legibility and accessibility with emojis, clear labels, automatically sized text, fonts designed for low vision, and screen-reader support, making the board easier to see, understand, and use for every user.
Simplified distribution with a stable download link that always serves the latest release, sparing users from hunting for the right version.
Evaluated commercial communication apps, found mostly ad-supported novelty software unsuitable for care use, and built a focused alternative that works offline, has no ads, and collects no data.

Gathered requirements from caregivers and prioritized by urgency, pinning critical phrases ("Something's wrong," "Call the doctor") on every screen and returning to the home screen automatically after inactivity, putting urgent needs one tap away.
Delivered v1.0 on two platforms in 13 days and kept shipping to 156+ issues, 168+ pull requests, and 8+ releases, turning caregiver feedback into 130+ shipped changes.

Tailored features to real care situations: a large-text Show mode that flips upside down for someone sitting across from the user, a hold-to-unlock caregiver lock that prevents accidental edits, and warnings when a tap would make no sound, preventing accidental edits, silent taps, and hard-to-read screens.

Investigated routing app audio directly into phone calls after a real speakerphone test showed call audio filtering drowned out the app, then shelved the feature after weighing feasibility, misuse risk, and texting as a simpler existing alternative, sparing users an unreliable feature and avoiding its misuse risk.
Protected irreplaceable recordings with a weekly backup reminder that never blocks the board.
Implemented a CI coverage gate that fails the build if core code drops below 90% line coverage (currently 91-99.5%), keeping the core logic protected as the app kept growing.

Wrote an automated smoke test for the live website that loads the production build, taps a tile, checks for errors, then stops the server and confirms the app still works offline, catching a broken release as soon as it goes live.
Introduced screenshot regression tests for the board and every dialog in portrait, landscape, and dark theme, making visual changes visible in each pull request.

Built upgrade testing into the release checklist: installed each new version over the previous one and confirmed recordings, boards, and settings survived, protecting users' irreplaceable recordings through each update.

Audited which tests CI actually ran, using Claude Code to look for gaps, and uncovered that half the UI test suite was failing unnoticed because CI never ran it, then repaired the tests and added emulator-based UI testing to CI, closing a blind spot that let UI regression defects slip past a passing build.

Diagnosed and fixed a race condition that could silently save stale data, and proved the fix with a regression test that fails reliably without it, protecting users' saved boards from silent data loss.

Automated UI tests for screen rotation, touch gestures, and accessibility font scaling, alongside testing on physical devices and emulators, catching real layout and input problems on the screens people actually use.

Configured GitHub Actions CI with branch protection and parallel Android and web jobs, requiring lint, tests, coverage, a documentation check, and the build to pass before any merge, keeping broken code off the main branch.
Converted caregiver feedback into tracked issues and paired every fixed defect with a regression test, making every report traceable from complaint to fix to test.

Designed data-integrity safeguards: older saved boards keep loading after format changes, tiles with missing audio reset themselves instead of failing silently, and cleanup never deletes audio a saved board still uses, protecting users' recordings and boards through updates and cleanups.

Explored the app hands-on and found layout breaks in landscape mode, fixed the header height, tile layout, and sticky rows, and tested both orientations from then on, keeping the board usable in both landscape and portrait.

Turned a caretaker's feedback on a demo (no way to say a phrase that wasn't pre-recorded) into on-the-fly text-to-speech, custom voice clips for tiles, and a full-screen Show mode for loud or quiet environments.

Directed Claude Code through a governed workflow (issue to feature branch to pull request to CI gate) to ship a cross-platform Kotlin app of 17,500+ lines of code and tests across 195+ commits, reaching v1.0 in 13 days without skipping review or testing.

Led a 4-phase migration to Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform, sharing about 80% of the code between Android and the web (WebAssembly) with no change in behavior on Android, letting one shared codebase power both platforms.

Owned architecture decisions and reviewed all AI-generated changes, including a single save path for all data, format migrations that keep older boards working, and interface-based designs testable on every platform, keeping the AI-written code correct, consistent, and maintainable.
Refactored a 2,900-line file into 8 focused modules in a planned pass with no change in behavior, keeping AI-generated code maintainable.

Combined an AI coding agent, generative voice synthesis (ElevenLabs), and on-device text-to-speech into one product that also plays recorded human voices, giving the user natural-sounding speech with a fallback that always works.

Delivered a maintainable handoff: user documentation, architecture docs, automated tests, CI, a fully automated signed-release pipeline, and a wiki that a workflow keeps in sync with the docs on every merge, letting anyone support the app without relying on its original builder.

Synchronized the wiki with the docs and README on every merge and added a bot that flags any pull request changing what users see without updating the user guide, keeping documentation current without manual effort.

Released the project as open source under Apache-2.0 with license and attribution notices for bundled audio, fonts, and icons, plus contributing, security, and code-of-conduct guides and issue templates, making the project safe for others to reuse and contribute to.

Diagnosed intermittent CI hangs in the browser test suite, tracing them to a UI test clock that stepped one frame at a time and an animation that kept re-arming itself, then fixed the test harness so a 16-run stress test went from 6 hung runs to 16 of 16 passing.

Traced an intermittent offline failure in the live-site smoke test to a real caching gap in the web app, then fixed the app as well as the test and forced the slow-load case on every run, making offline use reliable for every user.
Added a documentation check to the required CI gate that fails on any broken link, anchor or file path the docs name (107 paths verified at launch), catching stale docs before users do.

Built safeguards into the automated release pipeline (version and tag match, signing-certificate pinning, a stop on missing secrets) and proved them with dry runs before the first automated release, preventing a bad release from ever reaching users.

Automated releases end to end: pushing one version tag builds, signs, verifies, and publishes the Android app to GitHub Releases and the web app to GitHub Pages, with v1.0.1 shipped entirely by the pipeline, making every release faster and more consistent.
Automated dependency maintenance with Dependabot, which groups updates by release train each week and merges them only after the required checks pass, landing 11+ updates with no manual merges.

Extended the app to iOS with native audio, recording, speech, and file storage on one shared Kotlin codebase (about 89% of each app's code is shared), compiled and tested on the iPhone simulator in CI, readying the app for iPhone users as soon as a developer membership is in place.

Wrote and updated an AGENTS.md brief that tells any AI assistant or human contributor where code goes, how to keep three platforms in step, the required workflow, and known pitfalls, giving every new session current project rules from the outset.

Shipped picture and emoji tiles with hideable captions, plain spoken-name suggestions, and picture support in the large-text Show mode, softening the user experience by letting people recognize a tile by its picture, even from across the room.
Shortened the picture buttons for small phone screens while screen readers still announce the full phrases, keeping the editor usable for blind users.

Shielded saved boards and backups by making the new tile fields optional and giving pictures the same backup and cleanup protection as voice recordings, letting users update without risking any data or configuration loss.

Hardened the new picture and emoji tile enhancements with 45 automated tests and a follow-up sweep for edge cases like pictures that load late or go missing, catching regression defects before any user could hit them.
Developed picture tiles once in the shared code, bringing them to Android, the web, and iOS in a single change and cutting the work to one codebase instead of three.
Prioritized performance by shrinking pictures and loading them one at a time, keeping boards full of full-size phone photos fast and stable.

Designed a public Playwright suite that renders every resume version from the site's own data files and checks each one against the skills and bullets it should show, catching missing or wrong resume content before it goes live.

Proved the portfolio site's test suite could fail by deliberately breaking the site with a dead link, a missing heading, a truncated PDF, pale text, and players that load on their own, confirming the right tests caught each one and giving a passing build real meaning.
Automated accessibility scanning with axe across every page in light, dark, and phone width, plus keyboard checks, catching accessibility barriers before visitors hit them.

Configured GitHub Actions to run the suite on every pull request and a smoke test against the live site after each deploy and weekly, catching broken changes before they merge and live-site problems that appear between deploys.
Established an issue-first workflow in which every change ships through a reviewed pull request and merges only after the build check passes, making every change reviewed, traceable, and tested.

Launched a public portfolio site on Astro and GitHub Pages that serves as a filterable record of software, audio, and art work and renders role-specific resumes from one set of data files, giving prospective employers and clients one place to see everything.
Showcased the engineering process by keeping the repository public, turning how the site is built, tested, and shipped into a portfolio piece.
Documented how to add each kind of content in plain-language guides beside the data, making a new resume bullet, project, art piece, or release a data-and-image update instead of a code change.

Translated validation rules into plain-language build errors that name the file and field to fix, and mapped each YAML file to its schema for in-editor autocomplete and checking, making content mistakes quick to find and fix before they reach the live site.

Prioritized accessibility for every visitor with a bundled legible font, light and dark themes that follow system settings, a skip link, required alt text, and pages that keep working without JavaScript, making the site usable regardless of ability, device, or settings.
Chronicled how the site was built in a public project page and README covering the problem, the build, the stack, and the outcome, letting reviewers follow the reasoning and not just the result.

Modeled resume content as one set of data files (roles, bullets, skills, and versions) that renders the web resume, a print layout, and a PDF for each role-specific version, preventing the outputs from drifting apart.
Catalogued development, audio, and art work in three filterable archives that still work as plain lists without JavaScript, making a growing body of work easy to browse for every visitor.

Scripted PDF generation for each resume version with headless Chromium, failing the build when a PDF is missing, broken, or longer than two pages, protecting every PDF a recruiter downloads from being broken or too long.

Codified the site's content rules as schema checks that fail the build with readable messages, including single-hyphen copy, no phone numbers, past-tense bullet verbs, resolvable references, and required alt text, keeping rule-breaking content from ever reaching the live site.
Derived test expectations from the same YAML files the site is built from, eliminating a second hand-copied list that can go stale and keeping every test accurate as the content changes.

Safeguarded navigation and layout with a crawl that checks every link, anchor, and image and flags orphaned pages, plus layout checks that keep the header and gallery cards aligned, catching broken links and misaligned pages before visitors could spot them.
Reconciled the README with the project through an automated check of commands, links, files, and described tests, keeping the documentation trustworthy as the project changes.
Orchestrated Claude Code to launch this site, keeping ownership of design, review, and content decisions with tests and CI as the guardrails, delivering a complete, well-tested site.

Instituted repository rules that require a pull request and a passing build check before a change can merge, backed by auto-merge, automatic branch cleanup, and weekly Dependabot updates, protecting the main branch while keeping dependencies current with no manual effort.
Standardized a README check on every pull request, with a template checkbox and a written workflow step, keeping documentation in step with the code instead of drifting from it.

Created a guided Claude skill that checks new resume bullets against the same content rules the site build enforces, previewing errors and repeated-verb warnings before writing anything, making new content quick to add and hard to get wrong.

Reorganized the site's navigation into clearer menus, with redirects from the old addresses and tests guarding the new structure, making a growing body of work easier to find without breaking old links.

Generated a two-page resume for every one of six job types from one set of tagged bullet data, using an automated tool that finds the fewest cuts needed, replacing hand-editing with a build that enforces the page limit.

Imported private resume bullet data into public site files with a repeatable tool that stops before writing anything when it finds a bad entry, tested on made-up data so private notes stay private, keeping mistakes and private details off the live site.
Linked every one of 760+ Playwright tests to a labeled GitHub requirement issue with acceptance criteria, tying every test to the requirement it protects and leaving no test without a purpose.

Built a script that joins Playwright results with GitHub issues into a traceability matrix showing every requirement, its linked tests, and their latest results, published on the live site and in every CI run summary, making requirement coverage visible to anyone at any time.

Created a CI gate that fails the build when a requirement has no test and no written reason, a test cites a missing or retired requirement, or a test has no tag, surfacing coverage gaps in the pull request instead of after release.
Tested the checks as well as the product, breaking coverage and breaking tags on purpose to confirm the gate caught both, proving the traceability gate can be trusted.

Closed coverage gaps a traceability report exposed, writing new tests where a requirement needed one and recording a written reason where manual testing was the right call, leaving no unexplained gaps.

Caught a traceability report understating linked tests (491 of 634) by checking the live page after release, traced it to a de-duplication step that collapsed parametrized tests sharing a title, and fixed it with a test that fails on the old counting, keeping the published coverage numbers accurate.

Automated API and contract tests for the project totals the site pulls from GitHub, with 47+ Playwright tests (mocked on every pull request, live weekly) that validated every response against JSON Schema contracts, protecting the site's totals from malformed or missing data.

Covered failures a happy-path check misses, from missing fields and wrong types to rate limits, 5xx responses, network failures, and token leakage, making an unusable API answer fail clearly instead of writing broken data.
Verified the API checks themselves by deliberately breaking the data they guard and confirming each break was caught, demonstrating they catch real problems.
Wrote a Postman collection to run with Newman in the weekly workflow, catching and fixing a generator bug that made the site's commit count read as 1.

Created an evaluation suite that measures how reliably AI drafts resume bullets, scoring repeated runs of fixed prompts against coded content rules and failing the build if the pass rate drops below 95%, turning a prompt or model change into a number instead of a surprise.
Proved each automated check could fail before trusting it, deliberately breaking the code, data, or prompt it guards and confirming the right tests failed, giving every passing build real meaning.

Uncovered 10 embellished details by reading all 40 AI-drafted bullets by hand after they earned a perfect automated score, then added a manual review list to every report, keeping AI-drafted resume claims honest.
Distinguished service outages from quality drops and ran the evaluation weekly and on prompt changes, keeping an outage from being mistaken for a quality problem and catching silent model changes.

Budgeted AI usage by capping every evaluation run at 60 calls on a low-cost model, for under a cent per run, and keeping the API key in a GitHub secret, letting the suite run weekly without cost surprises or exposed credentials.
Tested the evaluation suite itself with 53+ tests that run without the API, catching real bugs in how it handles failures and keeping the suite's results dependable.
Created automated page-speed checks with Google's Lighthouse that run on every site change, protecting visitors from slowdowns and keeping every page at Lighthouse's top performance score of 100.
Created a load test (k6) that simulates visitors and confirms the site responds without errors in under 3 milliseconds, giving every future change a speed baseline to stay within.
Fixed a font-loading problem that made page content shift as it appeared, cutting the shifting by over 99% and keeping pages steady while visitors read.

Stabilized the page-speed check by switching it from a calculated estimate of a slow connection to a real slowed-down connection, making every pass or fail reliable while keeping the speed limits strict.
Designed a performance check to run only on site changes and stay optional, saving about 5 minutes on every unrelated pull request and never blocking work that doesn't touch the site.
Resolved a Windows-versus-server difference that incorrectly flagged saved resume layouts as out of date, ending false build failures and making the resume build behave the same on every machine.

Constrained a Claude Code reviewer to read-only access and had it audit the test suite for coverage gaps and weak checks, then tested its advice with a deliberately weak test before trusting it, giving the suite a skeptical second opinion without letting the AI change a line of code.

Tightened the test suite through about 16 fixes drawn from the Claude Code reviewer's findings, removing flaky waits, strengthening tests that could not fail, and widening checks to whole pages, making every passing build more trustworthy.

Chartered exploratory testing sessions on the live site, directing Claude Code through a controlled browser and recording what was covered, found, and left untested, then turning every finding into a test that failed before the fix and passed after, ensuring none can return unnoticed.

Guarded the public site against leaking private material with automated tests that fail the build if a private section, file, or phone number appears, enforcing privacy rules automatically on every change.

Hardened automated dependency updates with a 3-day waiting period and auto-merge only after the build passes, plus a weekly Claude routine that repairs failing updates but never merges, keeping upkeep nearly hands-off without giving the AI the final say.
Led QA across project teams of up to 20, coordinating onshore and offshore testers through daily handoffs spanning multiple time zones, keeping testing momentum consistent between shifts.
Streamlined Agile SDLC reporting for sprint-based teams, improving story tracking and resource allocation for globally distributed teams.
Built and maintained Confluence repositories that standardized repeatable testing processes across teams, giving testers one trusted place to find how each of those processes was run.

Explored features hands-on alongside scripted test cases, catching wording, grammar, and name and address display problems that met the spec as written, filing defects as they surfaced and raising them in stand-ups so the requirements were updated and fixes shipped.

Audited on-screen copy from multiple business, design, and development teams, catching wording and grammar errors and filing them as defects, protecting the accuracy and consistency of customer-facing text across teams.

Challenged requirements based on learned experience, drawing on US customer expectations and advocating for them in stand-ups until the requirements were corrected, presenting customers' details the way they expect to read them.

Owned end-to-end testing for a site serving 70M monthly visitors plus native iOS and Android apps, across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, with Internet Explorer as needed) in desktop, tablet, and mobile.

Staffed launch war rooms for device launches and peak retail events, validating live in production during the highest-revenue windows of the year and confirming the biggest sales days ran as designed.
Led testing for redesigns of high-traffic eCommerce purchase flows, improving stability and reducing call center volume.
Tested and launched new products, plans, features, and promotional discounts supporting customer acquisition and retention.
Owned governance for a Jira instance with 10,000+ users, establishing request and approval workflows that cut unauthorized feature additions by 90% within three months.
Analyzed confirmed fraudulent transactions to reverse-engineer attack patterns, then built test cases covering those and similar vectors so future releases were validated against known exploits.

Validated fraud-related fixes across test environments, production, and regression cycles, confirming every exploit stayed closed in later releases and shielding customers and revenue from repeat attacks.

Monitored application error logs in Kibana from the war room at every device launch and peak retail event, escalating live production issues to development and operations teams while the launch was still underway, limiting customer impact during the highest-traffic days.
Built Kibana dashboards and saved searches the team used for error monitoring and defect investigation, giving testers one place to spot trouble and trace its cause quickly.
Investigated defects through Kibana error logs and filed them with log evidence, giving developers concrete detail to act on.
Spotted patterns across recurring errors and used post-deploy log checks to confirm fixes held in production, exposing defects that had not truly been fixed and escalating them as larger issues.

Validated 20 third-party subscription integrations end to end, using Postman to confirm subscription status and service tier against each partner's API, and SQL to verify the matching subscription and customer IDs stored on Verizon's side, confirming both companies' records agreed before customers relied on them.

Tested the full subscription lifecycle in SQL, including activation, pause, tier changes, cancellation, and resubscription with existing or new customer details, confirming every stage was recorded correctly and each customer's subscription history stayed accurate and traceable.

Coordinated with partner teams to resolve data discrepancies between Verizon and partner test environments, working around partner sync jobs that lagged by minutes or hours or failed outright, and caught major issues before they reached production.

Created Confluence guides and recorded training sessions that got new onshore and offshore testers productive in about a week, and walked product owners and PMs through testing workflows across DevTools, Kibana, databases, CRM, and employee-facing systems.

Set the team standard for defects and test cases written with minimal assumptions (preconditions, detailed steps, expected and actual results, and visual evidence), reducing rejected and reopened defects.
Enforced requirements traceability by linking every defect to its test case and requirement, making it quick to tell whether the defect, test, or requirement was at fault.
Educated product owners on the distinction between defect severity and business priority, leading to more accurate defect triage.
Consolidated Jira labels from thousands of inconsistent variants to a couple hundred owned labels, routing defects to the teams responsible for fixing them.
Restricted label editing to a small group and published a self-service Confluence guide for requesting access and new labels.

Built credit-check test coverage from scratch in about two weeks for the device installment plan launch, partnering with credit, billing, and data teams to create test customers across credit classes.
Applied risk-based boundary testing and a code walkthrough with developers to give a documented conditional sign-off when there wasn't time to test every combination.

Authored requirements and acceptance criteria for an internal mock-customer data retrieval tool and worked with developers to strengthen test coverage, giving testers up-to-date and realistic customer data through tabbed field groups and fields searchable by name or ID.

Validated discount stacking on launches in a discount configuration tool, finding gaps between how testers read a discount and how it was actually configured, often showing the discount was set up correctly and the requirement was misunderstood, which cut false defects.
Wrote eCredit and Jira user guides that reached tens of thousands of views, reducing repeat questions across teams.
Managed test cases in Zephyr and then qTest, Verizon's primary test case management tool for more than eight years, keeping every test case organized and traceable to its defects and requirements.

Synced test cases across teams with shared Google Sheets on several projects, preventing stale copies, duplicate work, and conflicting results when test data or requirements changed ad hoc outside the formal tools.

Wrote test plans that defined scope by environment, flow, and platform (web, app, or both) and estimated the resources needed to cover it, giving QA and project managers a realistic basis for staffing and scheduling.
Defined defect assignment and escalation paths in the test plans and required traceable, repeatable defects backed by evidence, ensuring every defect had a clear owner and a path to resolution.
Simulated man-in-the-middle and cross-site scripting attacks with Burp Suite as part of fraud testing, probing for session-hijacking and script-injection weaknesses before real attackers could.

Inspected network logs, session data, cookies, and mobile browser behavior in Chrome DevTools during testing, pinpointing whether a failure came from the page, the network, or the server before filing it.
Executed automated test cases from a Selenium suite through a browser UI to validate flows, enhancing coverage of critical flows and reducing the manual testing needed.
Traced defective test cases and defects back to misunderstood or flawed requirements, getting every requirement corrected at the source so testers and developers worked from the same expectation.
Tested 10+ major releases and 20+ minor releases and device launches every year, plus priority fixes and content updates, protecting a site serving 70M monthly visitors.

Selected targeted regression suites of 50+ test cases from a pool of thousands, matching coverage to the flows every release touched and keeping regression cycles focused on what could actually break.

Wrote, maintained, and ran 100+ end-to-end manual regression test cases on large projects, choosing the flows and parameters every project needed and giving big releases full coverage of the paths that mattered.

Validated every way customers paid, from cards, PayPal, and ACH to gift cards, account credit, and split payments, across checkout, bill pay, and AutoPay, keeping revenue flowing through launches and peak retail events.

Proved card authentication held across the full 3D Secure, address, and security code matrix on Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Discover, making sure that only verified cardholders' payments were authorized.

Matched every payment outcome against the customer's screen and its Kibana status code across checkout, bill pay, and AutoPay, preventing a payment from showing as approved unless it actually went through.
Produced and engineered dozens of recordings from a home studio with a separate live room, all released and streamed publicly, delivering professional-sounding music at a great value to artists.
Performed on several releases in addition to producing and engineering them, picking up parts artists hadn't practiced or couldn't play in the time allotted, keeping sessions moving.
Designed studio signal routing through a patchbay, preamps, and audio interface, and moved all processing in the box, making every session fully recallable across projects that stretch over months.
Built session templates scaled to project scope and standardized mix prep (effects off, faders at unity, everything panned center), giving every project a consistent, repeatable starting point.

Diagnosed signal problems by tracing weak or degraded audio through the chain, such as clearing a healthy microphone by testing it directly into a preamp and confirming bad patch cables as the cause, avoiding an unnecessary replacement.
Performed guitar setups and soldering repairs on clients' instruments and amps, fixing problems on the spot and saving clients weeks of repair downtime and significant cost.
Learned and configured unfamiliar effects on request mid-session, researching and experimenting so artists could keep recording without delays.
Programmed humanized MIDI parts for VST instruments during recording sessions, making virtual instruments sound like live players.
Produced and engineered all studio projects in Studio One, my primary DAW since 2011, drawing on deep knowledge of how it runs and a large set of shortcuts to move through sessions quickly.
Organized an annual charity music festival for 11 years as one of three volunteer organizers, raising about $2,000 each year for Y'all Rock Camps, an inclusive music camp program.

Managed venue booking, band selection and scheduling, sound and gear, and promotion for a 20-band festival with audiences up to 400, plus about 10 smaller shows a year, delivering well-oiled shows and a community that keeps bands returning year after year.
Structured planning for the festival by establishing and refining the booking, scheduling, and promotion processes, giving the event a repeatable playbook it has run on for over a decade.
Designed the festival to stay low-cost, maximizing exposure for local bands while still returning surplus to charity.

Set clear, upfront expectations with performers: paid out-of-town bands fairly, asked local bands to donate their time, and directed all surplus to the charity, building trust and avoiding disputes over money.
Sped up stage changeovers by encouraging gear sharing between bands and helping performers load on and off stage, keeping a 20+ band lineup on schedule.
Provided on-the-spot technical support for performers unfamiliar with shared gear, troubleshooting setups under time pressure between sets, keeping every set on schedule.

Replaced a paper-based personnel change-of-status process, which required walking forms around for signatures, with SharePoint digital forms and automated approvals for an HR team serving 400+ employees, cutting turnaround from days to hours.

Gathered feedback from HR and IT stakeholders, assessed feasibility, and implemented approved changes, then handed off unfinished features as a documented backlog with the project, keeping development momentum going after the internship ended.
Trained HR users and developers in person, and wrote both user and technical guides, helping HR adopt new processes and the team support them.

Built a local replica of Nucor's SharePoint server on Windows Server to deploy and test web parts, restoring it weekly from a saved image, letting the team test safely without touching the live system and start every test from a clean state.
Tracked down and restored overwritten source files in a project without real version control, protecting the team's work.
Served as technical support for a 6-person project team, diagnosing slow machines and incorrectly installed software, keeping the team's work moving instead of stalled on technical problems.
Developed VB.NET forms and SharePoint web parts that drove the approval workflow and business logic through SQL procedures, giving HR approvals that ran automatically without manual routing.
